strengths: Large-scale, well-curated dataset (489K + 165K) addressing genuine gaps in visual reasoning supervision (limited multi-round CoT, 2D-only annotations)
Thoughtful dataset design with adaptive multi-round zoom strategy, clear annotation format, and systematic global-to-local reasoning supervision
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (Visual-CoT, MME, V*Bench) with strong results and thorough ablation studies
Novel depth-aware supervision through monocular depth and semantic segmentation, extending beyond prior 2D-only approaches
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation specs, training configurations, algorithms, and prompt examples in appendix
Broad domain coverage (text/doc, fine-grained, general VQA, spatial reasoning) with good annotation quality and human evaluation results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: training approach is standard SFT with LoRA; contribution is primarily dataset curation and scale rather than methodological innovation

Pseudo-3D annotation quality concerns: monocular depth is inherently uncertain; no ground-truth validation; impact of depth errors on reasoning not quantified; unclear if noisy depth supervision helps most tasks

Heavy GPT-4 dependence for annotations introduces bias, reproducibility concerns, and questions about whether models learn visual reasoning or GPT reasoning patterns; minimal inter-annotator agreement discussion

Unfair baseline comparisons: VISREASON models benefit from iterative multi-round zoom while baselines use single-step prediction; should either fine-tune all baselines on equivalent data or isolate dataset effect
Weak 3D grounding performance (0.276 grounded ratio) suggests models struggle with explicit grounding despite depth supervision; limited failure analysis of why grounding remains challenging
Insufficient ablation of depth contribution: no clear isolation of value from depth vs. better rationales; unclear which tasks benefit from 3D supervision; missing per-domain analysis
Very limited human evaluation (30 raters × 20 examples = 600 annotations for 489K dataset) without inter-rater agreement metrics or statistical significance testing
Dataset heavily derived from Visual-CoT (limited novelty in source); modest improvements on external benchmarks (MME: 0.777 vs. InternVL 0.848) suggest limited generalization and transfer

strengths: Addresses a genuine gap with large-scale multi-round visual reasoning supervision (489K examples, 4 domains) that existing datasets lack
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (Visual-CoT, VISREASON-PRO, MME, V*Bench) with ablations and human studies
Clear presentation with well-designed figures and thorough supplementary material (prompts, training configs, data examples)
Pragmatic dataset design with adaptive zoom strategy that avoids unnecessary cropping for simple cases
Depth-informed annotations (VISREASON-PRO) provide additional supervision signal for spatial reasoning
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: zoom-and-verify paradigm already explored in Visual-CoT; training is standard SFT+LoRA on existing Qwen2.5-VL with no architectural or algorithmic innovation
Unfair experimental setup: VISREASON models can use zoom tool in evaluation while baseline models (Table 2) cannot, making comparisons non-comparable and inflating relative improvements
Severe single-model bias in dataset: all reasoning traces generated by GPT-4.1; no validation that traces are 'human-like' or represent diverse reasoning patterns

Overstated depth-grounding claims: relies on monocular depth estimation (inherently unreliable) and semantic segmentation as pseudo-GT; Table 4 comparisons unfair since VISREASON-PRO was explicitly trained on grounding while baselines were not
Mixed generalization results contradicting claims: InternVL-2.5-8B outperforms VISREASON-PRO on MME (0.848 vs 0.777); V* improvements are modest; cherry-picking of successful benchmarks
Inconsistent ablations: adding Adaptive Zoom hurts performance on Doc/Text domain (0.908→0.856), suggesting design choices not well understood
Dataset construction not reproducible: relies on non-open-source GPT-4.1 models; unclear quality control, filtering criteria, and consistency checks beyond 'verify-and-fix'
Domain imbalance issues: GQA comprises 33% of dataset, Flickr30k 26%; no analysis of overfitting to dominant domains or justification for composition choices
Weak human evaluation: only 30 raters on 20 samples per method insufficient for robust conclusions; LLM-based grader lacks inter-rater reliability reporting

Missing critical analysis: no failure case discussion, bias analysis, or validation that depth predictions align with real 3D structure; limited comparison with recent CoT work (Insight-V, Chain-of-Focus 2025)

strengths: Large-scale, multi-domain dataset (489K examples) addressing genuine gaps: insufficient scale, lack of multi-round supervision, and minimal depth-aware grounding
Cognitively-aligned multi-round supervision with human-like global-to-local reasoning, differentiating it from prior single-step approaches (V*, VPD, Visual CoT)
Incorporation of 3D spatial grounding via pseudo-depth and semantic segmentation, extending beyond purely 2D annotations

Comprehensive experimental validation: strongest open-source MLLM on Visual-CoT (0.807), ablation studies isolating contributions, human evaluation on grounded faithfulness and clarity, generalization to external benchmarks (MME, V*Bench)
Excellent reproducibility: detailed training configurations, full prompt designs, algorithms, and supplementary material (26 pages) supporting potential dataset release
Well-motivated problem and clear presentation with effective visualizations and concrete examples
weaknesses: 3D grounding performance substantially underwhelms given its emphasis as core contribution: grounded ratio only 0.276 (27.6% of objects explicitly grounded), depth error 0.266 on [0,1] scale; limited analysis of why depth supervision underperforms or whether pseudo-labels are sufficiently reliable

Pseudo-3D annotations based on monocular depth estimation (Depth-Anything V2) and semantic segmentation (Mask2Former), not ground truth; no evaluation of pseudo-label quality or failure modes, raising questions about dataset reliability for 3D reasoning
Algorithmic novelty limited to straightforward supervised fine-tuning with LoRA and multi-round zoom-verify strategy; primarily a data contribution without methodological advances

Generalization gaps: notable performance drop on V*Bench (0.603 vs 0.807 on Visual-CoT); underperformance vs. Qwen-2.5-7B on text/doc tasks (e.g., TextVQA 0.922 vs 0.952) suggests task-specific limitations

Limited analysis of what drives improvements: Table 6 ablation provides only aggregate scores; no per-domain/per-task breakdown or error analysis; unclear which supervision components (multi-round, spatial, depth) provide most benefit
Data generation relies entirely on LLM-generated annotations (GPT-4.1-series); human validation is indirect (on final model outputs, not raw annotations); risk of systematic biases from LLM
User study modest in scale (20 items, 30 raters); no inter-rater agreement statistics or significance testing reported
Substantial training data advantage (654K examples) compared to baselines makes isolating dataset quality vs. scale benefits difficult
No computational cost analysis: multi-round inference is more expensive than single-pass, but latency/throughput trade-offs not discussed; unclear when multi-round reasoning is necessary
Missing comparisons: no direct quantitative comparison with other recent multi-round reasoning datasets (e.g., ARGUS, CogCom); limited discussion of distinguishing factors

strengths: Large-scale, multi-domain dataset (489K + 165K examples) addressing real gaps in visual CoT resources: scale, multi-round supervision, and depth-aware spatial reasoning
Thoughtful annotation design with global-to-local workflow reflecting human visual reasoning; adaptive zoom-in strategy preserves efficiency
Rigorous validation: comprehensive human audit (2,200 examples with confidence intervals), calibrated automatic evaluator (r=0.758), user study with 30 raters, multiple evaluation suites
Technically sound methodology with clear algorithms, proper coordinate transformations, and principled iterative refinement strategy
Strong improvements on targeted tasks: fine-grained recognition (+0.150 on CUB), spatial reasoning (+0.307 on Open Images), consistent ablation validation
Comprehensive supplementary material enabling reproducibility: all prompts, training configurations, implementation details, human audit results
Honest discussion of limitations including cascading localization failures, rationale quality issues, pseudo-depth noise, and Text/Doc performance trade-offs
weaknesses: Cascading localization errors remain unresolved: no recovery mechanism when initial RoI misalignment traps reasoning in irrelevant regions; no quantification of failure frequency or impact

Domain-specific gains, not universal transfer: Text/Doc performance degrades (0.920→0.892), source-removal ablation reveals massive dependency on domain-relevant training data, InternVL transfer shows mixed results (improvements on CUB/Open Images but degradation on GQA, Visual7W, VSR)
Rationale quality concerns: only 86.5% necessity and faithfulness in audit; Text/Doc particularly weak (70.9%, 71.9%); acknowledged mismatch between local crops and global reasoning requirements
Pseudo-depth labeled as '3D-grounding' but provides only ordinal cues from noisy monocular estimation; no analysis of error propagation; coordinate re-normalization under cropping under-specified
Heavy dependence on GPT-4.1-series for annotation generation creates circular reasoning bias and potential LLM artifacts; variability between VisReason (4.1-Nano) and VisReason-Pro (4.1-Mini)
Computational cost of multi-round inference not addressed; no timing comparisons despite clear efficiency trade-off; practical applicability limited despite accuracy gains
Limited failure mode analysis beyond cascading errors; no systematic error categorization; second-backbone transfer shows inconsistent generalization across tasks
Evaluation format mismatch (multi-round vs. direct-QA) suggests improvements may be format-specific rather than representing genuine reasoning capability gains
